title: Randomized client scripting and repeatability checklist for throughput runs
content:
Purpose:
This working note captures a repeatability-first approach for throughput benchmarking using randomized client scripts. It focuses on reducing hidden variance (client RNGs, session affinity, thermal drift), structuring load profiles that exercise batchers and caches, and a concise run-checklist and post-run analysis flow for deterministic claims.

High-level principles:
- Make the load generator as a programmable client (session semantics, pinned conversation ids, explicit KV prefix priming) rather than opaque request spammers.
- Separate deterministic anchors (anchor workloads) from randomized perturbations. Anchors are the canonical short sequences used for comparisons; perturbations are randomized interleaves for realism.
- Treat device state (SM clocks, fans, PCIe lanes) as part of experiment state; include thermal-soak phases.
- Use seed hygiene: run every configuration with 3+ random seeds and one seed==0 anchored run. Track RNG seeds in metadata.

Loadgen design notes:
- Client model: N sessioned clients, each with a sequence length distribution and TTL. Session affinity toggles (true/false) should be a parameter.
- Request families: prefix-primed (to exercise KV cache hits), cold-prefix (no priming), large-context (long KV growth), short-chat (low token responses).
- Inter-arrival patterns: deterministic steady (for baseline), jittered Poisson (realistic), microburst lattice (for microburst stress). Combine these streams to produce composite stress.

Example programmable snippet (pseudoconfig):
- clients: 64
- sessions_per_client: 8
- seed: ${SEED}
- profile_mix: [ {"name":"anchor-short","pct":20}, {"name":"primed-long","pct":30}, {"name":"microburst","pct":10}, {"name":"jittered-chat","pct":40} ]
- jitter_sigma_ms: 20
- session_ttl_s: 1200
- prefix_priming_tokens: 128
- kv_primer_mode: "round-robin"

Priming & conditioning procedure (recommended):
1) Thermal soak: 10–15 minutes with a light steady stream (~10% of target throughput) to stabilize clocks and fans. Record GPU temperature baseline.
2) KV primer pass: execute prefix-primed requests distributed across sessions to populate common KV entries. This pass should be deterministic (use seed 0).
3) Warmup ramp: linear ramp from 10% to target over 3–6 minutes with the anchor workload to allow internal caches, batchers, and memory allocators to stabilize.
4) Cool-check: pause 30s and sample traced events (alloc/free spikes, CPU steal). If large anomalies, abort and collect logs.
5) Main run(s): run the randomized profile for the configured duration. Repeat across seeds.

Observability signal list to collect (minimum):
- Token-level latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99/p999)
- Per-request kernel-level timings (where available)
- GPU util / SM occupancy / active SM cycles
- GPU memory used and transient alloc patterns
- Host CPU sys/user/steal and network transmit/receive throughput
- PCIe traffic counters if available
- Loadgen-side timing and client queue depths
- Model batch size distribution and effective tokens-per-batch time series

Repeatability checks and statistical heuristics:
- For each config, compute the per-run mean throughput and p99 latency. Require that the coefficient of variation (std/mean) across seeds < 3% for throughput to assert repeatability.
- Use bootstrapped 95% CI on median latency; overlapping intervals across configs means no statistically significant difference.
- Track drift within run: split the run into windows (e.g., 60s) and assert slope near zero for throughput and median latency after warmup.
- Flag runs where tail latency shows step changes coincident with background GC or kernel evictions.

Post-run forensic checklist:
- Attach GPU profiler capture (nsight/tegrastats/traces) abbreviated to first/median/last windows.
- Export batch histograms and a sample of raw request traces for p99 events.
- Correlate host-side scheduling spikes with latency spikes (look for CPU steal/gov changes).
- Compare anchor-run and randomized-run metrics to ensure anchor still matches historical baseline; if not, annotate environmental changes (driver, kernel, power cap).

Quick run checklist (what to do before claiming a reproducible throughput number):
- [ ] Confirm machine invariants: BIOS/driver, power cap, colocation, composable memory not reconfigured.
- [ ] Thermal soak completed and baseline temps recorded.
- [ ] KV primer completed with seed 0 and primer log saved.
- [ ] Run matrix executed (3 seeds + seed 0 anchor) and results uploaded.
- [ ] Metrics captured: perf counters, GPU metrics, loadgen traces, driver logs.
- [ ] CI post-process scripts executed to compute CV, bootstrap CI, and windowed-slope checks.
- [ ] Attach run-notes summarizing anomalies and commit ID for bench-runner.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add an automated detector for 'batcher starvation' by inspecting tokens-per-batch time series (Marco to prototype).
- Evaluate whether round-robin KV priming skews cache eviction patterns on quantized paths (Priya).
- Decide on a canonical seed set for long-term benchmark claims.

Appendix: short example of an analysis output (mocked):
- config: q8-trl-20k, target-throughput=1500 TPS, duration=30m
- seeds: [0, 7, 42]
- throughput mean cv across seeds: 1.7%
- median latency (ms): seed0=23.4, seed7=23.6, seed42=23.2 -> bootstrap 95% CI on median [22.8, 24.1]
- p99 latency drift slope: 0.02 ms/min -> accept
- verdict: reproducible under current infra; attach traces and bench-runner commit 4f2a9b

Notes: this is a working doc intended to standardize ad-hoc hacks we keep repeating. Keep it lightweight and copy the checklist into run-specific runbooks when claiming publishable numbers.
